entries.title: Isaiah 10:1
segments:
vv 1-4. 
 
  Woe unto them--his hand is stretched out still; the first four verses of this chapter are a continuation of the preceding discourse, and should not be separated from it.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:3
segments:
Come from far? from a distant nation, meaning the Assyrians. 
 
  Leave your glory? deposit it for safe-keeping.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:4
segments:
Without me; forsaken by me. 
 
  Under the prisoners--fall under the slain; under their condition, that is, among them. 
 
The strength of nations, as of individuals, depends on God's presence and help.  When he forsakes them they are without power, and fall an easy prey to their enemies.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:5
segments:
O Assyrian; or, "Woe to the Assyrian."  Here a new prophecy begins. 
 
  Rod of mine anger; rod which I use in my anger. 
 
  Is mine indignation; while they use it, I direct it for the execution of my vengeance upon the wicked.  The judgments threatened in
were executed mainly by the Assyrians.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:7
segments: God overrules the actions of wicked men for the accomplishment of his wise and good purposes, in such a way that they are left free to follow their own inclinations.  Thus he glorifies himself and advances the interests of his kingdom, while their responsibility and guilt are in no way diminished.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:9
segments:
Is not Calno as Carchemish? have I not destroyed both alike? 
 
  Calno; Ctesiphon of the Greeks, on the eastern bank of the river Tigris. 
 
  Carchemish; Cercusium, on an island in the Euphrates, at the mouth of the river Chebar. 
 
  Hamath; a large city of Syria on the river Orontes, called by the Greeks Epiphania. 
 
  Arpad; another city of Syria.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:10
segments: Found; found and plundered, as one finds a nest.
Graven images did excel; their guardian deities were stronger than those of Jerusalem and Samaria, yet they could not resist my power.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:12
segments:
Fruit of the stout heart; proud actions proceeding from it. 
 
The mighty conqueror who makes the world tremble at the sound of his name, receives all his strength from above; and when God has through him accomplished his whole work of chastisement, he humbles him as easily as he had exalted him, and gives him up a helpless captive to the power of his enemies.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:14
segments: Moved the wing--opened the mouth--peeped; made any show of resistance.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:15
segments: Lift up--no wood; "lift up that which is not wood," means, lift up the rational man; that is, as if the staff should wield the man, instead of the man the staff.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:16
segments: Fat ones; strong warriors.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:17
segments:
The light of Israel; that is, God. 
 
  His Holy One; Israel's Holy One.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:18
segments:
His forest--fruitful field; all his pomp and power. 
 
  Both soul and body; utterly. 
 
  As when a standard-bearer fainteth; which is the signal or flight to the whole army.  But we may better render, "as when a sick man pines away."

entries.title: Isaiah 10:19
segments: Write them; write their number.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:20
segments:
vv 20-24. 
 
It has been true of God's church in all ages, that "they are not all Israel, which are of Israel."  She has needed and received from the hand of God many sore judgments; but the effect of these has always been, not her destruction, but her purification and increased prosperity.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:21
segments: The remnant shall return; in the original, "Shear-Jashub," an allusion to the prophetic name of Isaiah's son.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:22
segments: The consumption; the destruction of the wicked in Israel.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:24
segments:
Therefore; since God's purpose is to use the Assyrian not to destroy, but to purify his people. 
 
  After the manner of Egypt; as the Egyptian taskmasters smote the Israelites of old.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:25
segments: The indignation--and mine anger in their destruction; in the destruction of the Assyrians.  Compare

entries.title: Isaiah 10:26
segments: Rock of Oreb;
Upon the sea; when Israel came out of Egypt, first to divide it, and then to overwhelm Pharaoh's host in its waters.
Every interposition of God for his people in past time, is a pledge of like interpositions in time to come, so far as needful for their safety and welfare.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:27
segments: Because of the anointing; of the Messiah to the office of King over God's people,
; which implies their deliverance from the yoke of their enemies.  But some render, "because of fatness;" that is, of Israel's renewed vigor.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:28
segments:
vv 28-32. 
 
  He is come to Aiath; the prophet in vision sees the Assyrian aproaching Jerusalem from the north, where all the places here mentioned were situated. 
 
  Michmash; a city lying near Gibeah, on the edge of a narrow passage or defile running east and west. 
 
  Hath laid up his carriages; as unable to transport them across the passage.  Carriages is equivalent to the modern word "baggage." 
 
  Nob; a city of priests.
It probably lay in sight of Zion.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:33
segments:
The bough; the pride and glory of the Assyrian king, who is compared to a lofty tree. 
 
  High ones of stature; his strong warriors, represented in this and the following verse under the figure of a forest of tall cedars. 
 
vv 33-34. 
 
In the history of this world, God has often arrested the proud conqueror in the very zenity of his power, and sent him back with shame to his own land; and he will do so again, whenever the interests of his church shall require it.

entries.title: Isaiah 10:34
segments: A mighty one; a mighty hewer, probably the angel who smote the Assyrian camp.
